_comment: The /data contract, declared once so both sides can be checked against it.
The firmware emits these field names in handleData(); the frontend reads them by
name. Nothing used to check the two agreed - they simply lived in one repo and one
build, so a rename broke loudly. Once the frontend versions and deploys
independently that stops being true: a renamed field becomes a blank gauge in the
car and a green test suite on the bench, which is the failure mode this project
So this file is the contract. firmware/test checks it against handleData() in both
directions, and web/ checks that every field the frontend reads is declared here.
Adding a PID means adding it here too, deliberately, in one place.
Field semantics are documented in README.md; units are SAE J1979's.

top.ok: a sample is fresh enough to render
top.seq: published-sample counter - the page counts these, not fetches
top.age: milliseconds since the sample was published
top.error: why ok is false; absent when it is true

_q_comment: The sampling receipt, emitted on both the fresh and the stale path.
A sibling of v, not a member of it. v is the car's readings; these are the
board's own account of how well it managed to read them, and mixing the two
would put a number the ECU never sent through the same staleness and warning
The point of publishing it: no consumer OBD tool shows the sample rate it is
actually achieving, so a logging interval set to 0.1 s and a value that moves
once a second look the same from the outside. Here the numbers already existed
and only went to the serial log.

q.cycleMs: measured duration of one full SAMPLE_ORDER pass
q.batchMs: how long the last bus exchange took
q.staleMs: the hold window derived from cycleMs - past this a batch is dropped
q.hz: achieved published-sample rate; null until a pass has been timed
q.bAge: per-batch age in ms, one per batch; null where a batch has never answered
q.share: a scan is taking most of the bus, so the sampler is on its slow share

boot.reason: how this run started: power | wake | panic | brownout | wdt | ...
boot.wakes: deep-sleep wakes since the last cold boot

scan.scan: a DID sweep has the bus
